profiles.description: Authenticated hosted inspection and diagnosis through an operator-scoped Azure identity.

providerPrerequisites.description: Azure Resource Manager and Resource Graph are available to the selected managed identity.
Resource providers needed by the resources being inspected are registered by the operator.

identity.trustBoundary: An authenticated caller reaches a hosted service whose operator-managed Azure identity is the only source of provider credentials.
rbac: Reader-equivalent ARM and Resource Graph access is granted only at operator-selected Azure scopes.
Effective-permission queries are allowed when AZURE_VERIFY_RBAC is enabled.

authorization.scope: Provider requests are constrained by the operator allow-list and the managed identity's effective Azure RBAC.

lifecycle.freshness: Azure reads query the provider for each operation; bounded RBAC results may be cached for the configured TTL.
lifecycle.cleanup: Provider clients and in-memory RBAC cache state end with the capability process.

notReady.reason: Readiness is not established until Azure authentication, a read-only provider query, and configured RBAC checks succeed.

profiles.description: Authenticated hosted Azure operations with separately enabled mutations, previews, confirmation, scoped RBAC, and provider verification.

providerPrerequisites.description: Azure Resource Manager and Resource Graph are available to the selected managed identity.
Every resource provider required by an authorized operation or Bicep template is registered by the operator.

identity.trustBoundary: An authenticated caller reaches a hosted service; operator and optional deployment managed identities remain operator-owned and are the only source of Azure credentials.
rbac: Reader-equivalent access plus only the explicitly enabled restart, start, or tag actions is granted at operator-selected scopes.
When generic Bicep deployment is enabled, a separate deployment identity receives template-specific write access at an allow-listed scope.
Role-assignment deployment requires separately granted privileged RBAC and is never implied by provider access.

authorization.scope: Provider requests are constrained by operator allow-lists, distinct operation and deployment identities, and effective Azure RBAC.

lifecycle.freshness: What-if and provider reads are authoritative at request time; confirmation hashes expire and RBAC results use a bounded TTL.
lifecycle.cleanup: Temporary Bicep workspaces are removed after compilation and deployment locks expire or are released.

notReady.reason: Readiness fails when provider authentication, selected mutation RBAC, deployment RBAC, compiler, or durable deployment store requirements are unusable.

mutation.authorization: MUTATIONS_ENABLED is off by default; Azure allow-lists and effective RBAC independently constrain every consequential operation, and DEPLOYMENTS_ENABLED separately gates Bicep execution.
mutation.confirmation: Constrained operations support dry-run and require explicit confirmation; Bicep execution additionally requires a fresh matching what-if confirmation hash and a reason.
mutation.authoritativeVerification: Verify constrained operations by reading the affected ARM resource and Bicep operations through Azure deployment status and operation APIs; production Bicep execution independently requires durable Azure Table records.
